sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the layout pieces, icons, navigation, shared colours and spacing, and shared parts such as cards, badges, chips, buttons and section headers.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup for the screen's look.

sections.name: ReportViewerScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Report header and AI summary box
sections.what: Shows the back and share buttons, the report name, lab, doctor and date, and a fixed AI summary paragraph with a warning that it is not medical advice.
sections.why: Likely reason: a layout sketch of how a finished report should look to a patient.
sections.watch_out: The summary text is typed in, so it will not match a real report until it is replaced with real data.

sections.name: ReportViewerScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Key values list and action buttons
sections.what: Lists four blood values with their normal ranges and a normal badge, then shows two buttons, Share with Doctor and Ask Maate AI. Neither button does anything yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: placeholder values and actions that are not yet connected.
sections.watch_out: Every value is fixed as normal, so a real abnormal result would not appear on this screen.

summary: A fixed demo screen showing a blood test report, a sample AI summary and four key values. Its content is typed into the file, not loaded from anywhere.
purpose: Shows what a finished report view should look like. In this version the report data is not connected.
why: Likely reason: an early layout or placeholder for the report view. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Draws a back button and title, then a card with the report name, lab, doctor and date, then an AI summary box with a fixed paragraph, then a list of four blood values with their normal ranges and status badges, then two buttons. The buttons and the share icon do nothing when pressed.
inputs: None. Every value is written directly in the file.
outputs: A static screen. No data is read, saved or sent.
risks: The screen shows realistic-looking results, doctor and lab names. A user could mistake them for their own results. All buttons and the share icon do nothing.
debug: If every report shows the same blood values, this is expected because the data is fixed. To make the screen real, the file would need to load data from the store or the API, which this file does not do.
